canonical_topic: Bid placement between own cost and the next unit's cost
definition: Generators typically place bids above their own break-even cost but below the break-even cost of the next more expensive plant type in the stack.
core_idea: This spacing lets a plant capture margin above its own cost while still positioning itself to clear ahead of costlier competitors, and it lets an outside observer bracket a plausible bid range for each plant type.
key_points: Example given: a coal plant with an $50 break-even cost, sitting just below an $85 break-even unit, would likely bid somewhere between $50 and $85
Predicted consumer demand (plotted against price) determines which plant ends up being the price-setter
relationships: Determines the marginal provider in the dispatch stack
trading_implications: Bracketing a plant's likely bid range using the break-even costs of neighboring stack units helps forecast the clearing price at a given demand level
